blocks.text: Service Advisor — Diploma in Automobile Engineering

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Engineering, Technology & Computing
EDUCATION PATHWAY
Diploma in Automobile Engineering
Typically a 3-year diploma after Class 10, depending on the institution and entry route.
CAREER AREA
Automotive Service & Customer Relations
Vehicle servicing, repair coordination, customer communication and workshop operations.

A Service Advisor is the link between vehicle owners and the service workshop. The advisor understands customer concerns, records vehicle complaints, coordinates inspections and repairs, explains estimates and keeps customers informed until the vehicle is ready for delivery.
The role combines automotive knowledge, communication, customer service, documentation and service-sales skills.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Welcome customers and record vehicle details and reported issues.
Conduct or coordinate initial vehicle inspections.
Prepare job cards and explain recommended services.
Communicate repair estimates, timelines and additional work requirements.
Coordinate with technicians, workshop supervisors and spare-parts teams.
Obtain customer approval before proceeding with chargeable work.
Monitor repair progress and communicate delays.
Explain completed work, invoices, warranties and maintenance schedules.
Handle customer complaints and follow up after service.

blocks.label: Common workplaces
blocks.text: authorised automobile dealerships, multi-brand service centres, commercial vehicle workshops, two-wheeler service centres, fleet maintenance companies and electric vehicle service centres.
Stage 1 — Class 10
Build foundations in mathematics, science, communication and basic computer applications.
Stage 2 — Diploma in Automobile Engineering
Study vehicle systems, engines, transmission, brakes, suspension, automotive electrical systems, diagnostics and workshop practices.
Stage 3 — Workshop exposure
Learn job-card preparation, vehicle inspection, repair estimation, customer handling and service-centre workflows through supervised training.
Stage 4 — Entry-level employment
Target Service Advisor Trainee, Junior Service Advisor, Workshop Customer Relations Executive or Service Coordinator roles.
Year 1 — Automotive fundamentals
Focus on understanding vehicles and developing professional communication.

items.text: Learn the basic construction and operation of automobiles.
Understand engines, transmission systems, brakes, steering and suspension.
Study basic automotive electrical and electronic systems.
Learn vehicle components, tools and workshop safety.
Develop spoken and written communication in English and relevant regional languages.
Practise computer fundamentals, spreadsheets and professional email writing.

blocks.text: Practical assignments

items.text: Prepare a labelled diagram of a vehicle's major systems.
Create a basic vehicle inspection checklist.
Practise explaining routine maintenance to a customer.
Prepare a sample vehicle intake form.

blocks.text: Year 2 — Vehicle servicing and customer handling
Focus on service-centre processes and repair coordination.

items.text: Understand preventive maintenance and periodic service schedules.
Learn the purpose of engine oil, filters, coolant, brake fluid and other service items.
Study common vehicle complaints and the diagnostic process.
Understand job cards, labour operations, spare-parts estimates and service invoices.
Learn warranty basics, service history and customer approval procedures.
Practise handling complaints, delays and customer questions professionally.

blocks.text: Practical assignments

items.text: Prepare a sample job card from a fictional customer complaint.
Create a service estimate with labour and parts listed separately.
Draft a customer update message about a repair delay.
Prepare a delivery checklist for a serviced vehicle.

blocks.text: Year 3 — Service operations and job readiness
Focus on handling the complete customer service journey.

items.text: Learn workshop scheduling, technician allocation and repair-status tracking.
Understand diagnostic reports and how to communicate technical findings clearly.
Study customer satisfaction, complaint resolution and service follow-up.
Learn dealership management software concepts and digital service records.
Practise explaining estimates, obtaining approvals and managing expectations.
Complete an internship or in-plant training at an automobile dealership or service centre.
Develop sales ethics, negotiation, time management and teamwork.

blocks.text: Final-year project ideas

items.text: Customer service workflow for an automobile workshop.
Vehicle maintenance reminder and follow-up tracker.
Service-centre customer satisfaction survey and analysis.
Workshop appointment scheduling spreadsheet.
Dashboard tracking service turnaround time and customer feedback.

rows.text: Engine, transmission, brakes, suspension, steering and cooling
Batteries, charging systems, sensors and electronic control units
Periodic service schedules, fluids, filters and wear-item checks
Interpreting customer symptoms and coordinating professional diagnosis
Accurate complaint descriptions, inspection findings and repair instructions
Labour charges, spare-parts costs, taxes and customer approvals
Warranty terms, service history and escalation procedures
Active listening, explaining technical issues and setting expectations
Technician allocation, parts availability and delivery timelines
Complaint handling, follow-up, satisfaction and ethical service recommendations

blocks.text: A Service Advisor should not promise a diagnosis or repair outcome before the technical team has assessed the vehicle.
Dealer Management System (DMS)
Learn job-card creation, service history, estimates, invoicing, appointments and customer records in the system used by the employer.
Automotive diagnostic tools
Understand the purpose of OBD diagnostic scanners, fault codes and workshop inspection reports. Actual diagnosis should be performed by trained personnel within their responsibilities.
Excel and reporting
Track appointments, repair progress, pending approvals, customer follow-ups and service turnaround time.
Customer communication tools
Use approved CRM systems, email, telephone and messaging platforms to communicate estimates, approvals and delivery updates professionally.
Passenger Vehicle Service Advisor
Coordinates routine servicing, repairs, estimates and customer communication at car dealerships and service centres.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students who enjoy cars, customer interaction and organised service workflows.
Commercial Vehicle Service Advisor
Coordinates maintenance and repair for trucks, buses and fleet vehicles, where downtime and service scheduling are important.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students interested in heavy vehicles, fleet operations and workshop coordination.
Electric Vehicle Service Advisor
Coordinates EV inspections, service bookings, diagnostic reports and customer communication about vehicle-specific maintenance.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students interested in emerging automotive technology and EV service processes.
Workshop Operations Coordinator
Coordinates appointments, workshop capacity, spare-parts availability, work-in-progress and vehicle delivery.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students who enjoy planning, team coordination and operational problem-solving.
Consider training that strengthens both technical knowledge and customer service.

blocks.label: Automotive service and maintenance
blocks.text: vehicle inspection, preventive maintenance and service procedures.

blocks.label: OEM or dealership training
blocks.text: brand-specific vehicle systems, warranty processes and service software, where available.

blocks.label: Automotive diagnostics fundamentals
blocks.text: diagnostic trouble codes, scan-tool reports and electronic vehicle systems.

blocks.label: Customer relationship management
blocks.text: complaint resolution, customer satisfaction and professional communication.

blocks.label: Excel and service reporting
blocks.text: estimates, appointment tracking, service records and performance reports.

blocks.label: EV fundamentals and safety awareness
blocks.text: EV components, charging systems and the importance of high-voltage safety procedures.

blocks.label: Professional communication
blocks.text: customer conversations, service explanations and conflict resolution.
Prioritise practical training and employer-recognised programmes. EV high-voltage work must be handled only by appropriately trained and authorised personnel.
Look for internships or trainee opportunities at:

items.text: Authorised automobile dealerships.
Multi-brand car and two-wheeler service centres.
Commercial vehicle workshops.
Fleet maintenance companies.
Electric vehicle dealerships and service networks.
Automotive repair chains and workshop management businesses.
Automobile manufacturers' service and after-sales departments.

blocks.text: During an internship, aim to learn:

items.text: How vehicles are received and customer complaints are recorded.
How job cards and preliminary estimates are prepared.
How technicians report diagnostic findings.
How customers approve additional repairs.
How parts availability and repair progress are tracked.
How invoices, delivery inspections and follow-up calls are managed.

rows.text: Service Advisor Trainee, Service Coordinator, Customer Relations Trainee
Senior Service Advisor, Warranty Coordinator, Workshop Controller
Assistant Service Manager, Customer Relations Manager
Service Manager, After-Sales Manager, Multi-site Service Operations Manager

blocks.text: Progression depends on customer-handling skills, technical understanding, service performance, experience and employer requirements.
Examples of organisations and industry groups to research include:

items.text: Automobile manufacturers and dealership networks such as Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, Mahindra, Hyundai and Toyota.
Two-wheeler manufacturers and service networks.
Commercial vehicle service centres and fleet maintenance businesses.
Electric vehicle manufacturers and their authorised service partners.
Multi-brand automobile service chains and independent workshops.

blocks.text: These are examples to investigate, not confirmation of current vacancies. Search official career pages and dealership recruitment channels for Service Advisor Trainee, Service Advisor and Workshop Coordinator positions. Check whether each role accepts diploma graduates and whether prior customer-service experience is preferred.
Suggested portfolio contents

items.text: Sample vehicle intake form and customer complaint record.
A job card based on a fictional vehicle issue.
A repair estimate separating parts and labour.
A service-delivery checklist.
A customer complaint-resolution scenario.
A spreadsheet tracking appointments and repair status.
An internship report describing the service workflow and tasks observed.

blocks.text: Use fictional customer and vehicle records for portfolio examples. Do not disclose dealership records, customer contact details or confidential service information.
Automotive after-sales service is expanding beyond conventional servicing. Service Advisors can build expertise in:

items.text: Electric vehicle service coordination.
Connected-vehicle diagnostics and digital service records.
Customer experience and after-sales operations.
Fleet maintenance and service scheduling.
Warranty administration and technical service coordination.
Workshop performance analysis and service process improvement.
Service management across multiple locations.

blocks.label: Recommended strategy
blocks.text: Build a strong understanding of vehicle systems, job-card processes and customer communication. Add dealership software, Excel and EV fundamentals to prepare for modern service-centre roles.
Tick off each milestone as it is completed.
Employability milestones
0 of 10
Understand major vehicle systems and periodic maintenance.
Learn workshop safety and vehicle inspection procedures.
Practise preparing job cards and recording customer complaints.
Create sample repair estimates and delivery checklists.
Develop clear customer communication and complaint-handling skills.
Learn Excel and basic service-reporting methods.
Understand warranty and customer-approval processes.
Complete dealership or workshop internship experience.
Prepare a resume and service-workflow portfolio.
Apply for suitable Service Advisor Trainee or entry-level roles.
Reset checklist
By the end of the diploma and practical training, a job-ready candidate should be able to:

items.text: Explain common vehicle systems and routine maintenance requirements.
Record customer complaints accurately and prepare clear job cards.
Coordinate inspections, estimates, repair progress and customer approvals.
Communicate technical findings in understandable language.
Maintain service records and use basic digital reporting tools.
Handle customer concerns professionally and ethically.
Work effectively with technicians, parts teams and workshop supervisors.

blocks.label: Best starting point
blocks.text: Gain practical experience in an automobile service centre, learn the complete vehicle-reception-to-delivery process and strengthen customer communication. Then specialise in passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles or EV after-sales service.
